Jacobson held the CEO position through 2005 and, since 2013, has been non-executive chairman.

name: Matthew Rabinowitz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Matthew Rabinowitz is the cofounder and executive chairman of clinical genetic testing and molecular diagnostics firm Natera.
He cofounded the Austin, Texas-based company in 2004 after his nephew died from a severe genetic condition six days after birth.
Rabinowitz and his cofounder Jonathan Sheena took the company public on the Nasdaq in 2015; he owns about 2% of the company's shares plus several options tranches.
In 2017, he cofounded clinical whole genome analysis platform company MyOme. The firm was valued at $187 million in December 2025 and Rabinowitz owns a 19% stake.
Born in South Africa to parents who were both doctors, Rabinowitz came to the U.S. in 1992 to attend Stanford University.

name: Daniel Dines
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Daniel Dines is cofounder and CEO of UiPath, a robotic process automation company that went public on the New York Stock Exchange in April 2021.
Dines started DeskOver in 2005 in Bucharest, Romania. He later renamed it UiPath and moved its headquarters to New York City in 2018.
Customers like Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui bank or Toyota North America can spend millions on UiPath's virtual "robot" that can automate complex, repetitive tasks.
An avid reader, Dines said in a 2019 Forbes cover story that he reads in the mornings, often not showing up to UiPath's office until 11 am.
UiPath recorded $1.4 billion in revenue and a net loss of $74 million in the fiscal year through January 2025.
forbes_facts: In October 2019, after a period of rapid hiring at UiPath, the company laid off more than 300 employees, or about 11% of its workforce.

name: Polys Haji-Ioannou
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Polys Haji-Ioanno is the son of late Cypriot shipping magnate Loucas Haji-Ioannou (d. 2008), who once owned the world's largest private tanker fleet.
Much of his wealth derives from a large stake in easyJet, the discount airline founded by his younger brother, Stelios.
Polys continues the family's shipping legacy with his own 13-tanker fleet.
He has also invested heavily in both commercial and residential real estate, particularly in Cyprus, Greece, Monaco and London.
forbes_facts: Haji-Ioanno's yacht, "Esmeralda," is named after one of the world's largest tortoises.
Haji-Ioanno remains involved in the philanthropic foundation started by his father.

name: Herriot Tabuteau
sec_insider_companies: Axsome Therapeutics, Inc. (AXSM) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Herriot Tabuteau founded Axsome Therapeutics in 2012 with the goal of developing life-changing treatments for the millions of patients living with brain disorders.
Tabuteau owns 15% of Axsome, which he took public in 2015.
Prior to founding the company, Tabuteau worked in healthcare finance, including as a partner at hedge fund Healthco/S.A.C. Capital.
He is the inventor on more than 200 patents, including potential new medicines for depression, behavior disturbances in Alzheimer's disease and narcolepsy.
Axsome's drug Symbravo (meloxicam and rizatriptan) received FDA approval in January 2025 for the acute treatment of migraines with or without auras.
Its drug AXS-05 for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease agitation received a Breakthrough Therapy designation from the FDA in 2020. It now plans to submit a supplemental new drug application for it.

name: Bastian Nominacher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Bastian Nominacher is cofounder and co-CEO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Nominacher owns a 16% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Nominacher's cofounders Alexander Rinke and Martin Klenk are also billionaires. Rinke is co-CEO and Klenk is CTO.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.
